groups.title: Precision Machining
groups.summary: Turnkey manufacturing of precision parts to your specification, on CNC and manual machines.
groups.intro: McCarter is a full service, start to finish precision machine shop. CNC and manual machines run alongside each other, so the same job can be set up for mass production or for the one off that no one else has. Our goal is to provide rapid and reliable precision work to enhance our customers' systems in a measurable way.

groups.title: Single Crystal Si
groups.summary: Single Crystal Si optics, structures and semiconductor components, made with patented and proprietary processes.
groups.intro: We manufacture Single Crystal Si components for the semiconductor and defense markets, and our success is possible due to the proprietary and patented processes we developed specifically for Single Crystal Si. We fabricate Single Crystal Si structures and optics with near zero surface damage and residual stress, net shaped and ready for optical finishing.
groups.imageAlt: A silicon wafer with a grid of microchip dies

services.title: Silicon Optics and Structures
services.text: Single Crystal Si optics and optical substrates, offered as the choice material even over beryllium, aluminum and zerodur, from small simple planar parts to large-scale and complex designs.
points: Does not creep or jitter over time or during use
Stable in dynamic vibration, cryocycling and nuclear exposure
Used in high power laser optics and telescope optics
Expertise began with a Silicon Validation Study in 1999

services.title: Patented Superfinishing
services.text: Conventional machining of a raw Single Crystal Si boule induces surface and subsurface damage. Our patented superfinishing method provides a finish ready for single point diamond turning and final polishing.
points: Near net shaped, reducing or eliminating lapping
Remaining damage removed by acid etching

services.title: Glass Frit Bonding
services.text: Our proprietary glass frit bonding method produces lightweight, large scale and complex Single Crystal Si structures and optics, built up beyond the size of an available boule.
points: Blanks built up to sizes in excess of one meter
Five-year plus optical stability performance record
Mirrors manufactured in four weight categories

services.title: Metal Inserts for Silicon
services.text: Frit bonded 39NiFe inserts attach Single Crystal Si optics directly into metal hardware, eliminating mounting cans, fixtures and the cost and weight that come with them.
points: Built-in flexure design for radial and torsional movement
Rigid inserts tested to NASA flight requirements
Joint designed to act as a metallurgical joint, not a mechanical one

services.title: Semiconductor Replacement Parts
services.text: We first fabricated silicon components in 1988 when a local semiconductor company needed replacement parts made from silicon for their silicon-pulling equipment in order to maintain purity.
points: Complex shapes with very close tolerances
Parts for the semiconductor and defense markets

about.title: A 10,000 sq. ft. shop fifteen minutes east of Houston.
text: McCarter operates a 10,000 sq. ft. clean, fully-equipped facility fifteen minutes east of Houston, Texas, with separate cleanroom, manufacturing, laboratory, etching, welding, painting and conferencing areas.

The McCarter team is a multi-talented, efficient workforce with the proven ability to provide fast response to the complicated and critical needs of our customers. Most of the team has been with McCarter for many years and have weathered the ups and downs of growing a small business. That can-do attitude has given us a reputation for accomplishing tasks that others hesitate to attempt.
In October 2021, MZA Associates Corporation acquired full interest in McCarter Machine, Inc. McCarter is operated out of its longtime La Porte, Texas facility as a Division of MZA.

facts.heading: Part of MZA Associates Corporation
facts.text: In October 2021 MZA Associates Corporation acquired full interest in McCarter Machine, Inc., a precision machining company specializing in the design and fabrication of complex Single Crystal Silicon light-weight optics and components as well as precision metal machining for heavy industries. McCarter is run as a Division of MZA from its longtime La Porte facility. MZA Associates Corporation is at 4900 Lang Ave NE, Suite 100, Albuquerque, NM 87109, (505) 245-9970, mza.com.

facts.heading: Starting material
facts.text: The key to stress-free Single Crystal Si components is the starting material, so we use only zero-defect, near perfect boules free of residual stress, which allows rapid machining with conventional CNC machines and tools. Boules are available from several suppliers to 300mm diameter and 800mm long, and frit bonding builds blanks up beyond one meter.

facts.heading: Why surface finish matters
facts.text: Damage on the surface affects thermal-optical properties such as transmission, absorption and reflection, and subsurface damage affects thermal-mechanical properties such as strength, microyield, hardness and fracture toughness. That damage reaches deeper than etching and polishing alone can remove, which is why the superfinishing method matters.

facts.heading: Independent testing
facts.text: All but a few of the tests on our Single Crystal Si samples were performed by independent universities and laboratories, so we have data on how our processing methods affect strength, dynamic response, cryostability, coating response, long-term stability and rad hardness.

facts.heading: Measured optical stability
facts.text: In September 2006 Dr. Dave Content of NASA Goddard Space Flight Center remeasured a lightweighted 19 kg/m2 Single Crystal Si mirror, 6.7" in diameter with a 6 to 1 aspect ratio and a 600mm aperture radius, that he bought from us in 2001. The 2001 measurement read P/V .410wv RMS .068 and the 2006 measurement read P/V .420wv RMS .070, so the mirror had no notable movement over five years.

facts.heading: Vibration testing
facts.text: A seven-piece cantilevered Single Crystal Si assembly, with two mirror surfaces finished directly on the structure and four frit bonded inserts, was vibration tested at Goddard Space Flight Center beside a monolithic aluminum structure. The relative measurement between the two optical surfaces changed by only 0.1 arcsecond horizontally and vertically.

facts.heading: Complex bonded assemblies
facts.text: One customer needed a 17" diameter Single Crystal Si assembly made of seven Single Crystal Si parts, with cooling passages, core drilled holes and slots and a hyperbolic contour. There were no failures across the bondlines, all of the cores remained intact, and the bonded planks machined as if they were monolithic.

facts.heading: Mirror weight categories
facts.text: We have manufactured lightweight mirrors in each of four weight categories, so a customer has flexibility when designing for payload requirements. QED Corporation removed 100% of the print-through on a Simplistic Lightweight Mirror in 90 minutes using their patented MRF process.

facts.heading: Why Single Crystal Si
items: Thermal and dimensional stability, and it does not creep or jitter over time or during use
A stable optic material from cryo to near 1100 C, with high thermal diffusivity
Blurr-free from 170K to 500 C, which qualifies it as the only optical material for endo/exo operational missions
Highly polishable and safe to handle, with no health hazards
Low thermal expansion, low density and high thermal conductivity
Excellent hardness and shock resistance, and low cost by volume
Used extensively in high power laser optics, and selected and qualified as the primary MEMS material
Not to be confused with polysilicon, amorphous silicon, silicon foam or silicon slurry, which show deficiencies in several thermal and structural properties

facts.heading: Why glass frit
items: Electrical insulation and hermeticity
High viscosity and low flow, which give good control of the bondline
Low reactivity, with no eutectics formed
Repair by refiring, and disassembly and reuse by high temperature or chemical means
Shown to withstand extreme temperature change, extreme vibration excitement and radiation hardening
Mirrors integrated into each other and mounted directly onto metal substrates, with no housings needed as a beryllium substitute would require
